caveats: Independent R/L variation implies joint diameter/length redesign for a uniform pipe.
A separate valve needs its own resistance calibration.
Changing cylinder geometry may change Cad unless compensated elsewhere.
A different fluid or mean pressure changes several material properties simultaneously.
A redesign affecting heat-transfer geometry needs reassessment/refitting of the thermal-loss impedance.
geometry_map.published_reduced_Lf_control: Valid published mathematical reference, but inverse uniform-pipe length is below the 2013 investigated range. Not a declaration of physical impossibility.
geometry_map.nominal_length_discrepancy: 2013 Table1 lengths inserted literally into L=rho*l/A give approximately twice Table3 cylinder inertances. 2011 defines inertial lengths as time-averaged liquid-column lengths; a half-filled interpretation is plausible but not explicitly reconciled in the inspected tables.

circuit_equivalence_audit.established_structure: Lure feedback: passive stable linear network and one static scalar tanh nonlinearity.
circuit_equivalence_audit.open_loop_input: w, dimensional thermal pressure in physical-time equation Cad*Pdot=(w-P)/Rth+U+V
circuit_equivalence_audit.open_loop_output: D, dimensional displacer hydrostatic pressure deviation
circuit_equivalence_audit.validation: Compare G at s=0.13+i*geomspace(0.01,1000,32) to component D of solve(s*I-A,b), where A is the dimensional five-state linear matrix with saturation replaced by input w and b=(1/(Rth*Cad),0,0,0,0). Nominal Table2 components used.
circuit_equivalence_audit.known_related_model: Sprott2000 Eq12: third-order tanh jerk equations, three equilibria.
circuit_equivalence_audit.non_equivalence_scope: The unique equilibrium of positive-parameter NTP prevents a global bijective conjugacy of the entire flow to those particular three-equilibrium examples. This is not a classification of local attractors, invariant reductions or all saturating-feedback circuits.
